title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear portions and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, it's essential to provide adequate iron and folate to ensure the health of both mother and baby. Iron helps prevent anemia, while folate supports fetal development. In this article, we'll introduce three simple and delicious recipes that combine iron with vitamin C, helping pregnant women have a nutritious and safe meal.

## Nutrient Analysis
Iron and folate are two crucial nutrients during pregnancy. Iron helps create hemoglobin, a protein in blood that carries oxygen to cells. Folate, or vitamin B9, helps prevent neural tube defects in the fetus. To enhance iron absorption, pregnant women should combine iron-rich foods with vitamin C-rich foods, such as lemons, oranges, or bell peppers.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Vegetable Bowl
* 100g grilled chicken
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1/2 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, green beans, bell peppers)
* 1 lemon
* Salt, pepper, and other seasonings

Grilled chicken is an excellent source of heme iron, while mixed vegetables provide vitamin C and folate. Lemon helps enhance iron absorption.

## Recipe 2: Beef and Water Spinach Stir-Fry Bowl
* 100g beef stir-fry
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1/2 cup water spinach
* 1 bell pepper
* Salt, pepper, and other seasonings

Beef stir-fry is a rich source of heme iron, while water spinach provides folate and vitamin C. Bell pepper helps enhance iron absorption.

## Recipe 3: Vegetarian Red Bean and Vegetable Bowl
* 1 cup cooked red beans
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1/2 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, green beans, bell peppers)
* 1 lemon
* Salt, pepper, and other seasonings

Red beans are an excellent source of non-heme iron, while mixed vegetables provide vitamin C and folate. Lemon helps enhance iron absorption.

## Food Safety Notes
During pregnancy, women should avoid eating undercooked or raw foods, such as sushi, sashimi, or undercooked meat. Additionally, they should limit foods high in salt, sugar, or fat.

## Conclusion
These three recipes provide a rich source of iron and folate, helping pregnant women have a nutritious and safe meal. For more delicious and safe recipes, women can visit our [meal planner](/planner) or [join our community](/blog/topics) to share experiences and receive support from other pregnant women.
